claim: For agent-based circuit explanation, imposing the explicit observe-then-hypothesise-then-causally-validate workflow is what makes explanations good, beyond the capability of the underlying model: both a dedicated observation step and the causal validation loop add accuracy, and the structured workflow beats an unconstrained coding agent with the same model. Supported only if removing either the observation stage or the validation loop lowers task-description accuracy for every one of four backbones, and lowers component-level scores in at least 14 of the 16 backbone-by-metric-by-ablation comparisons; and if, with the same backbone and context on a 31-circuit subset, the structured agent exceeds a general-purpose coding agent on both role accuracy and description quality without losing task accuracy.

experiments: Build the benchmark. Setup: take the 84 RASP-program models of InterpBench (Tracr-compiled, retrained with strict interchange intervention training so weights and activations resemble trained transformers, ground-truth circuits preserved), excluding the two IOI tasks because their circuit is widely published; trace each circuit component back to the RASP variable it implements and annotate a role tag (mapper 72, combiner 33, aggregator 32, indicator 15, router 11; 120 MLP and 43 attention components, 1.94 per circuit) plus a natural-language note, with five input-output examples per task. Metrics: tag exact match; description quality on a 0-2 scale and binary task-description correctness, each scored by GPT-5.4 and Gemini-3.1-Pro and taking the lower score; and code-execution success.

Define the agent. Setup: a LangGraph state machine that, per component, writes and executes an observation plan (TransformerLens helpers for attention patterns and activations), proposes a hypothesis without seeing the role taxonomy, writes and executes a validation plan (helpers for ablation, activation patching, interchange interventions) and decides support or refutation, feeding refuted hypotheses back; up to five execution attempts per stage and three hypothesis iterations per component, then tags each component with the taxonomy and writes a circuit summary and task description. Backbones: GPT-5.4, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Gemini-3.1-Pro and Qwen-3-Coder-30B-A3B.

Ablate the workflow stages. Setup: full benchmark; remove the observation stage (hypothesise directly) or the validation loop (pass the first hypothesis straight to classification). Result: task accuracy full / no observation / no validation 0.63 / 0.59 / 0.60 for GPT-5.4, 0.75 / 0.57 / 0.65 for Claude, 0.83 / 0.73 / 0.69 for Gemini and 0.25 / 0.23 / 0.24 for Qwen (drops of 1-18 points); the full pipeline is higher on component metrics in 14 of 16 comparisons (exceptions: GPT-5.4 description 0.46 vs 0.47 without observation, Qwen tag 0.67 vs 0.68 without validation).

Compare with an unconstrained coding agent. Setup: Claude Code with Claude-Sonnet-4.6 given the same context but no imposed workflow, on a 31-task, 55-component subset. Result: tag accuracy 0.811 vs 0.770, description quality 0.639 vs 0.603, task accuracy 0.767 for both, execution success 0.94 vs 0.69; on inspection, Claude Code ran a causal intervention in only 15 of 31 tasks, relied on observation alone in 12 and inferred the task from the examples without loading the model in 4.
